salient_findings: Painless, round, hazelnut-sized mass localized to the tail of the right epididymis
Solid, well-demarcated, hyperechoic, hypoperfused mass on scrotal ultrasonography
key_facts: 16-year-old male with no prior medical history
Noted a small lump in his right hemiscrotum two months earlier
Denies any history of scrotal trauma or inflammation
Lump's size remained unchanged over two months
Experienced mild discomfort during exercise, which resolved with rest
Testicles and groin were otherwise unremarkable on physical examination
Scrotal ultrasonography demonstrated a 1.3 × 1.1 cm mass at the tail of the right epididymis
Mass contained two small hypoechoic foci
Routine blood tests, coagulation profile, and serum tumor markers were all within normal limits

differentials: Malignant mesothelioma of the tunica vaginalis
per_call: Malignant mesothelioma of the tunica vaginalis

shortlist.label: Adenomatoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Most common benign tumor of the epididymis, matches the ultrasonography findings of a solid, well-demarcated mass

shortlist.label: Epididymal cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Common benign condition, could present as a painless scrotal mass, although the ultrasonography findings are not typical

shortlist.label: Spermatocele
shortlist.why_kept: Benign cystic lesion of the epididymis, could present as a painless scrotal mass, although the ultrasonography findings are not typical

shortlist.label: Lipoma of the spermatic cord
shortlist.why_kept: Benign tumor, could present as a painless scrotal mass, although the ultrasonography findings are not typical

shortlist.label: Epididymal adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare malignant tumor, cannot be ruled out without further investigation, despite the patient's age and lack of risk factors

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a painless, solid, well-demarcated mass at the tail of the epididymis, as demonstrated by scrotal ultrasonography, is consistent with an adenomatoid tumor, which is a common benign tumor of the epididymis.

rejected.label: Epididymal cyst
rejected.why: Epididymal cysts are typically fluid-filled and may not present as a solid mass on ultrasonography.

rejected.label: Spermatocele
rejected.why: Spermatoceles are cystic structures that contain sperm and are usually found at the head of the epididymis, not the tail.

rejected.label: Lipoma of the spermatic cord
rejected.why: Lipomas of the spermatic cord would likely have a different ultrasonographic appearance, with a more heterogeneous echo pattern due to the presence of fat.

rejected.label: Epididymal adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The patient's age, lack of systemic symptoms, and normal serum tumor markers make a malignant tumor like epididymal adenocarcinoma less likely.
